title: Innsbruck or Salzburg at Christmas: which Austrian city to choose
author: Matt
intro: Pick Salzburg for the grandest Christmas market, baroque squares and the story of Silent Night, and Innsbruck for markets in the mountains, with skiing and snow a cable car ride away. Here's how they compare for a December break.
seo_title: Innsbruck or Salzburg at Christmas? Markets compared
seo_description: Salzburg's main market runs 19 Nov 2026 to 1 Jan 2027 under the fortress. Innsbruck's markets sit below the Alps, with skiing nearby. Which to choose.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Best Christmas market:** Salzburg
- **Best for snow and skiing:** Innsbruck
- **December high:** about 3 to 4°C
- **Between them by train:** about 2 hrs

Both are compact, walkable cities with old towns that look made for Christmas. The difference is the setting: Salzburg is a baroque city of churches, palaces and music, while Innsbruck is an Alpine city with the mountains rising straight out of its streets.

sections.heading: Innsbruck and Salzburg side by side
sections.text:
| | Salzburg | Innsbruck |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main market | Cathedral and Residenz squares | Old Town, by the Golden Roof |
| Market dates | 19 Nov 2026 to 1 Jan 2027 | From mid-November, some into January |
| Setting | Baroque city below a fortress | Old town below the Alps |
| December high | about 4°C | about 3°C |
| Skiing | Resorts an hour or more away | Nordkette, from the city centre |
| Ideal stay | 3 nights | 3 to 4 nights |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our [Salzburg](/destinations/salzburg) and [Innsbruck](/destinations/innsbruck) guides.

sections.heading: Why choose Salzburg
sections.text:
Salzburg's **Christkindlmarkt** fills the squares around the cathedral and the Residenz, with Hohensalzburg Fortress lit up on the hill above. It's one of the oldest and best-known Christmas markets in the German-speaking world, and in 2026 it runs from **19 November to 1 January 2027**.

Beyond the main market, there are smaller ones to find:

- **Hellbrunn Palace**, whose courtyard becomes an Advent market with a forest of lit trees.
- **The fortress**, which holds its own Advent market on weekends.
- **Mirabell Palace**, in the square in front of the gardens.

The story of **Silent Night** belongs here too. It was first sung in 1818 in Oberndorf, a short trip north of Salzburg, where the Silent Night Chapel now stands. Add Mozart's birthplace and the Sound of Music sights, and three nights fill easily.

Local knowledge: Salzburg is busiest on Advent weekends, when coach groups arrive from Germany and Austria. If you can, visit the markets on weekdays.

sections.heading: Why choose Innsbruck
sections.text:
Innsbruck has several Christmas markets within walking distance of each other, and the setting does the work: snowy peaks tower over the rooftops.

- **The Old Town market**, below the Golden Roof, is the prettiest, with a giant Christmas tree in the narrow streets.
- **Marktplatz**, by the River Inn, is bigger and good for food and mulled wine.
- **Maria-Theresien-Strasse**, the main shopping street, with views up to the Nordkette.

The big extra is the mountains. The Nordkette cable cars start from the city centre, and in winter you can go from a Christmas market to snow-covered slopes in under half an hour. The ski season usually starts in December, so you can mix a day or two of skiing with the markets, though the snow is most reliable from January.

Watch out: Innsbruck's markets don't all keep the same dates, and some close before Christmas while others stay open to 6 January. Check innsbruck.info for each market's dates in 2026.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text:
Both cities have airports, but direct flights from the UK mostly run in the ski season, often at weekends, and change each winter. Many visitors fly to **Munich** instead and take the train, which takes about two hours to either city.

Salzburg and Innsbruck are about two hours apart by train, on the same main line, so you can combine them in one trip: two nights in each makes a good five-night Austrian Christmas break. Add a day trip to [Hallstatt](/destinations/hallstatt) from Salzburg if you have time, though it's popular even in winter.

sections.heading: So, which one?
sections.text:
- **Choose Salzburg** for the classic Christmas market, music and history, and the Silent Night story.
- **Choose Innsbruck** if you want snow, mountain views and the chance to ski.
- **Choose both** if you have five nights, with the train in between.

For more Christmas trips, see our [best Christmas markets in Europe](/blog/best-christmas-markets-in-europe), [Vienna or Prague at Christmas](/blog/vienna-or-prague-at-christmas) and the [Christmas holidays](/destinations/christmas-holidays) page. If you can't agree, add both cities to somewhere.party and let the draw choose.

faqs.question: When is the Salzburg Christmas market in 2026?
faqs.answer: The Salzburg Christkindlmarkt on the cathedral square runs from 19 November 2026 to 1 January 2027.

faqs.question: Is Innsbruck or Salzburg better at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Salzburg has the bigger, more famous Christmas market. Innsbruck has the better mountain setting and skiing close by. Both make a great three-night break.

faqs.question: Can you visit Innsbruck and Salzburg in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes. They're about two hours apart by train, so two nights in each works well.

faqs.question: Is there snow in Innsbruck at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Often in the mountains above the city, and sometimes in the streets too, but it isn't guaranteed. January has the most reliable snow.
